class: Any two test folders that are not Python packages and hold a test file with the same name break the whole test run with an import-file-mismatch collection error, but only after both files reach the same branch, so each PR is green alone and the break appears at merge time.
mechanism: pytest's default import mode inserts each test file's folder into sys.path and imports it by its bare module name; tests/rules/test_model.py and tests/strategy/test_model.py both import as 'test_model'.

first_seen.where: W-005 branch build/W-005-round3 after merging main (W-013 had added tests/rules/test_model.py)
first_seen.evidence: python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -> 'import file mismatch: imported module test_model has this __file__ attribute: tests\rules\test_model.py'; 1 error during collection. Each file passes alone (tests/strategy/test_model.py: 7 passed).

fix: Renamed W-005's file to tests/strategy/test_strategy_model.py; a spec-integrity test fails whenever two test files anywhere under tests/ share a name, so the collision is caught in the PR that introduces it.

detection.note: Only catches the collision once the colliding file is on the same branch as the other; a PR branched before the other merged still passes alone, but CI runs on the merge result, so the PR's own CI turns red before merge.
